R-1.name: Residential 1
R-1.purpose: The R-1 district is intended to accommodate single-family detached residential development on large suburban lots.

R-2.name: Residential 2
R-2.purpose: The R-2 district is intended to accommodate moderately compact single-family detached residential development in a low-density urban neighborhood context.

tableNotes.1: Residential dwellings are not permitted to front on arterial streets. Residential dwellings shall be permitted to front on collector streets if a rear-entry garage is provided.
tableNotes.2: Minimum of 20-feet for garages of front-entry residential dwellings.

R-3.name: Residential 3
R-3.purpose: The R-3 district is intended to accommodate a variety of compatible residential housing types including single-family detached, single-family attached, duplex, triplex, fourplex, small-scale multifamily, and live/work dwellings.

tableNotes.1: See §4.3.2.A: Cottage Development for additional height, setback, and density limitations for cottage developments.
tableNotes.2: See §4.3.2.D: Dwelling, Multifamily for minimum dwelling unit size requirements.
tableNotes.3: See §5.7.6: Neighborhood Transition Standards for additional setback and height limitations.
tableNotes.4: Minimum of 20 feet for garages of front-entry residential dwellings.

M-1.name: Mixed-Use Neighborhood
M-1.purpose: The M-1 district is intended to accommodate small- to medium-scale mixed-use development that supports a comfortable and safe bicycle and pedestrian friendly development pattern and that accommodates infill and redevelopment.

tableNotes.1: The area between the street back-of-curb and the inside edge of the public sidewalk shall be dedicated as public right-of-way or have a public access easement.
tableNotes.2: The build-to-line may be extended to accommodate one row of parking spaces in accordance with §5.5: Parking and Loading.
tableNotes.3: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.

M-2.name: Mixed-Use Suburban Corridor
M-2.purpose: The M-2 district is intended to accommodate a mix of small- to medium-scale mixed-use development that promotes sustainable infill and redevelopment of older commercial sites, while ensuring that the site design, uses, and scale are consistent with adjacent residential neighborhoods.

tableNotes.1: The area between the street back-of-curb and the inside edge of the public sidewalk shall be dedicated as public rightof-way or have a public access easement.
tableNotes.2: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.

M-3.name: Mixed-Use Urban Corridor
M-3.purpose: The M-3 district is intended to accommodate a mix of medium- to large-scale mixed-use development that supports pedestrian- and transit-oriented uses.

tableNotes.1: The area between the street back-of-curb and the inside edge of the public sidewalk shall be dedicated as public rightof-way or have a public access easement.
tableNotes.2: Activated outdoor patio areas serve as an extension of the building façade and may abut the build-to line.
tableNotes.3: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.

M-4.name: Mixed-Use Center
M-4.purpose: The M-4 district is intended to support the most intensive, transit supportive development to create a unique, mixed-use, and integrated regional destination.

review.uses: A maximum of 70 percent of the acreage of a proposed development may be used for residential or mixed-use with residential uses.

tableNotes.1: The area between the street back-of-curb and the inside edge of the public sidewalk shall be dedicated as public rightof-way or have a public access easement.
tableNotes.2: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.
tableNotes.3: Subject to the height limitations of the Airport Overlay District.

CL.name: Commercial Limited
CL.purpose: The CL district is intended to accommodate small-scale commercial, retail, office, service-oriented, and accessory uses.

tableNotes.1: Minimum of 10 feet when adjoining the R-1, R-2, R-3, or A zoning districts or Planned Developments that reference those zoning districts.
tableNotes.2: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.

CG.name: Commercial General
CG.purpose: The CG district is intended to accommodate medium- to large-scale commercial, retail, office, service-oriented, and accessory uses.

tableNotes.1: Minimum of 10 feet when adjoining the R-1, R-2, R-3 or A zoning districts or Planned Developments that reference those zoning districts.
tableNotes.2: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.
tableNotes.3: Buildings may exceed 70 feet in height if the additional height is set back from the setback line one additional foot for each two feet of height above 70 feet.

LI.name: Light Industrial
LI.purpose: The LI district is intended to accommodate a mix of light manufacturing, warehousing and distribution, auto-oriented uses, research and development operations, offices, showrooms, and a limited range of associated retail services, and accessory uses.

tableNotes.1: Minimum of 10 feet when adjoining the R-1, R-2, R-3, or A zoning districts or Planned Developments that reference those zoning districts .
tableNotes.2: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6.

AA.name: Addison Airport
AA.purpose: The AA district is intended to support and optimize operational efficiency of the Addison Airport and to support the airport’s role as a key economic engine for the Town and region.

tableNotes.1: Minimum of 10 feet when adjoining the R-1, R-2, R-3, or A zoning districts or Planned Developments that reference those zoning districts.
tableNotes.2: Buildings abutting a property in the R-1, R-2, or R-3 zoning districts shall comply with the neighborhood transition standards in §5.7.6: Neighborhood Transition Standards.
tableNotes.3: All buildings shall comply with FAA height standards and regulations.
